answer: Answers are salted with a 172 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the quartz salt is published after the ivory checkpoint, the thread audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 155 keys therefore burns for 155 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
